(2) Reduce motion — with prefers-reduced-motion:reduce emulated, .hero-kenburns and .hero-vignette both report 'animation: none' and 'duration: 0s'; the Landing H1 still renders (no layout break); prefers-reduced-motion CSS block in index.css:277-287 neutralises animations/transitions app-wide. Clicking triggers a scan; summary panel shows '21 contrast fail(s) — <n> checked'. 'Clear' button removes all dashed outlines (queried 0 remaining [data-a11y-flag]). Overlay is mounted at App.js:134 gated by NODE_ENV==='development' (dev-only, won't ship). (4) Alt text — Header account avatar alt="Jenn McDonald's profile photo" (Header.jsx:199 / Avatar.jsx:48). Profile page avatars carry 'Jenn McDonald's profile photo'; CommunityHub author avatars use the same pattern; PartnerEvents org falls back to icon when o.picture is null, Avatar aria-label='<org> logo' via fallback. MOBILE (Expo web preview): (1) Alt text — Home logo <Image accessibilityLabel="Sail More Now"> renders alt='Sail More Now'; Home hero ImageBackground uses accessibilityElementsHidden + importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants" and renders alt='' (non-accessible for AT). Avatar in ui.tsx:162, home logo (index.tsx:145), clubs logo (clubs.tsx:59), partner follower avatar (partner.tsx:145), event flyer (events/[id].tsx:140), hub photo (hub/[id].tsx:125), post photo (post/[id].tsx:110), directory work samples (directory/[id].tsx:140), PhotoPicker preview (PhotoPicker.tsx:37) — all confirmed with meaningful accessibilityLabel via grep. (2) Reduce motion — MotionModal wrapper (MotionModal.tsx) reads useReducedMotion() (hooks/useReducedMotion.ts subscribes to AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled + reduceMotionChanged listener) and forwards animationType='none' when reduced=true else falls back to caller's animationType ?? 'slide'. All 6 modal files verified via grep to import MotionModal as Modal: feed.tsx, directory.tsx, profile.tsx, my-events.tsx, crew-bank.tsx, index.tsx. Crew-bank page renders without red screen; prefers-reduced-motion:reduce is picked up by browser matchMedia (=True), which RN Web maps into AccessibilityInfo. No React Native red screens observed. Pre-existing 'shadow* deprecated' warning unrelated to this iteration.
critical_code_review_comments: A11yContrastOverlay.jsx: the Alt+Shift+C hot-key registers a window-level listener guarded by window.__a11yHotkey but never removed. Because the overlay is dev-only and mounted once at App root, this is fine in practice, but if the overlay is ever remounted (e.g. HMR test harness), it will still register only once thanks to the sentinel — good. Consider still attaching the listener inside a useEffect for cleanup symmetry.
A11yContrastOverlay.jsx line 193: onClick={() => (open ? scan() : scan())} — the ternary is redundant (both branches call scan()). Trivial cleanup.

A11yContrastOverlay.jsx: initial scan reports 21 contrast fails on Landing. This is informational (the overlay's job is to surface them). Consider a follow-up pass through the flagged elements — likely muted body copy on off-white bands and low-contrast pill text — though not part of this iteration.

index.css :focus-visible uses !important on outline + outline-offset. Necessary to beat the codebase's many Tailwind outline-none utilities and correct in intent, but flags a code smell (widespread outline-none). A future refactor could remove outline-none usages and drop the !important.

mobile app/index.tsx:142 uses ImageBackground with accessibilityElementsHidden + importantForAccessibility='no-hide-descendants'. On web the resulting gets alt='' which is correct AT-wise, but does not carry aria-hidden='true'. RN Web doesn't map accessibilityElementsHidden to aria-hidden. Not a blocker (empty alt already hides from AT); for extra safety on web a plain accessibilityLabel='' plus role='none' could be considered, but current behaviour is compliant.

MotionModal.tsx: passes through all ModalProps but sets animationType before spread ordering — 'return <Modal {...props} animationType={animationType} />' — good, animationType override wins. No issue.

success_rate.frontend: web 4/4 features verified; mobile 2/2 features verified via live check + code inspection
